questions.question: A, B and C can complete a work in x, 30 and 45 days, respectively. B and C worked together for 6 days. The remaining work was completed by A alone in 12 days. The value of x is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Time taken to complete the work by A = x days

Time taken to complete the work by B = 30 days

Time taken to complete the work by C = 45 days

Time taken to complete the work by B and C together = 6 days

Remaining work completed by A = 12 days

**Formula used:**

Work = Efficiency × Time

**Calculation:**

LCM of 30 and 45 is 90

Efficiency of B = 90/30 = 3 units/day

Efficiency of C = 90/45 = 2 units/day

Total units of work by B and C together = [(3 + 2) × 6]

⇒ 30 units

Efficiency of B and C together = (90 – 30) = 60 units

Efficiency of A = (60/12) = 5 units/day

Hence, A can complete the whole work in = (90/5) days

⇒ x = 18 days

**∴ The value of x is 18**

questions.question: R and S can finish a work in 10 days, S and T can finish it in 12 days and T and R can finish in 8 days. In how many days will the work be finished if they all work simultaneously?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

R and S can finish a work in 10 days

S and T can finish a work in 12 days

T and R can finish a work in 8 days

**Formula used:**

Work done by R and S in 1 day = 1/10

Work done by S and T in 1 day = 1/12

Work done by T and R in 1 day = 1/8

Let work done by R, S, and T in 1 day be r, s, and t respectively

r + s = 1/10

s + t = 1/12

t + r = 1/8

**Calculation:**

Adding the three equations:

(r + s) + (s + t) + (t + r) = 1/10 + 1/12 + 1/8

⇒ 2r + 2s + 2t = 1/10 + 1/12 + 1/8

⇒ 2(r + s + t) = 1/10 + 1/12 + 1/8

⇒ r + s + t = 1/2 × (1/10 + 1/12 + 1/8)

Calculating the sum:

⇒ 1/10 + 1/12 + 1/8

⇒ 12/120 + 10/120 + 15/120

⇒ 37/120

So,

r + s + t = 1/2 × 37/120

⇒ r + s + t = 37/240

The work done by R, S, and T together in 1 day is 37/240

Therefore, the number of days required to finish the work is:

⇒ 240/37

**∴ The correct answer is option 3 (240/37).**

questions.question: A and B can complete a piece of work in 27 days and 54 days, respectively. They completed the work in 9 days with the help of C. How many days will C take to complete eight-ninths of the work alone?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A and B can complete a piece of work in 27 days and 54 days, respectively. 

They completed the work in 9 days with the help of C. 

**Concept used:**

Work = efficiency × time

**Calculation:**

Total work = LCM [27, 54] = 54

∴ Efficiency of A = 54/27 = 2 units/day 

Efficiency of B = 54/54 = 1 unit/day 

Efficiency of (A + B + C) = 54/9 = 6 units/day

Efficiency of C = Efficiency of (A + B + C) - {Efficiency of A + Efficiency of B} 

Efficiency of C = (6 - {2 + 1}) = 3 units/day

Time taken by C to complete eight-ninths of the work alone = 8/9 × 54/3 = 16 days

**∴ The correct answer is 16 days.**

questions.question: Nirmal completed the school project in 45 days. How many days will Amit take to complete the same work if he is 25% more efficient than Nirmal?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Time taken by Nirmal to complete the project = 45 days

Amit is 25% more efficient than Nirmal

**Formula Used:**

Efficiency and Time are inversely proportional.

**Calculation:**

Let the efficiency of Nirmal be 100 units.

Then, efficiency of Amit = 100 + 25 = 125 units

Since Efficiency ∝ 1/Time, we have:

Time taken by Amit = (Efficiency of Nirmal / Efficiency of Amit) × Time taken by Nirmal

⇒ Time taken by Amit = (100 / 125) × 45

⇒ Time taken by Amit = (4 / 5) × 45

⇒ Time taken by Amit = 36 days

**Amit will take 36 days to complete the same work.**

questions.question: Pranjal takes twice as much time as Vikram or thrice as much time as Ashwin to finish a piece of work. Working together, they can finish the work in 6 days. Vikram can do the work alone in:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Time taken by Pranjal = Twice as much as Vikram

Time taken by Pranjal = Thrice as much as Ashwin

Time taken to finish work together = 6 days

**Calculation:**

⇒ Let Pranjal take x days to complete the work.

⇒ So, Vikram takes (x)/(2) and Ashwin takes (x)/(3) days to complete the work.

⇒ According to the question, all working together

⇒ Then, ((1)/(x)+(2)/(x)+(3)/(x) )=(1)/(6)

⇒ (6)/(x)=(1)/(6)

⇒ x = 36 days

⇒ Time taken by Vikram to complete the work = (x)/(2)=(36)/(2)=18 days

**Hence, Vikram can complete the work alone in 18 days.**

**Short trick:**

**Formula used:**

Efficiency = Total unit/No. of days

Time is inversely proportional to efficiency

**Calculation:**

As , we know that time is inversely proportional to efficiency 

So, let the efficiency of pranjal be x 

Then efficiency of vikram = 2x

Efficiency of Ashwin = 3x

Total efficiencies = x + 2x + 3x = 6x 

Total days taken to work together = 6 

Total unit = 6x × 6 = 36x

Now, vikram can do the work in = 36x/2x = 18

**Hence, vikram can do the work in 18 days .**

questions.question: A can finish a work in 15 days, B can finish the same work in 25 days. They work together for 5 days. The rest of the work is finished by A and C in 4 days. Then C alone can finish the work in:

Total Work Concept

Total Work is typically taken as the Lowest Common Multiple (LCM) of the given individual time periods. Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Time taken.

Efficiency and Time Relationship

The efficiency of a person is inversely proportional to the time taken by them to complete a piece of work. If the ratio of time taken is a:b, their efficiency ratio will be b:a.

Chain Rule (Group Work)

If M₁ men can do W₁ work in D₁ days working H₁ hours per day, and M₂ men can do W₂ work in D₂ days working H₂ hours per day, then (M₁ × D₁ × H₁) ÷ W₁ = (M₂ × D₂ × H₂) ÷ W₂.

questions.question: A and B working separately can do a piece of work in 21 and 24 days, respectively. If they work for a day alternately with A beginning the work, it would be completed in _________.
questions.solution:
Given:

A and B working separately can do a piece of work in 21 days and 24 days respectively.

Calculations:

Time is taken by A to complete the work = 21 days 

so part of the work done by A in 1 day = (1)/(21)

similarly, part of the work done by B in 1 day = (1)/(24)

Work done by (A + B) in 2 days = ((1)/(21) + (1)/(24)) = (15)/(168) = (5)/(56)th part of work

Work done by (A + B) in 11 pairs of days i.e.,

Work done by (A + B) in 22 day = (5×11)/(56)=(55)/(56)th part of work

Remaining work = 1 - (55)/(56) = (1 )/(56)th part of work

On the 23rd day, again A will work separately. So,

Time is taken by A to complete the (1 )/(56)th part of the work 

= (1)/(56) × 21 days 

= (3)/(8)

Total time taken = 22 + 3/8

∴ The correct answer is 22(3)/(8) days.

questions.question: P can complete five-eighths of a work in 15 days and Q can complete three-fourths of the same work in 30 days. They worked together for 8 days and then P left. How much time will Q working alone, take to complete the remaining work?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

P can complete five-eighths of work in = 15 days

Q can complete three-fourths of the same work in = 30 days.

**Calculation:**

P alone can complete work in = 15 × 8/5 = 24 days

Q alone can complete work in = 30 × 4/3 = 40 days

(P + Q)'s 1 day's work = 1/24 + 1/40 = 1/15

(P + Q)'s 8 days work = 8/15

Remaining work after 8 days = 1 - 8/15 = 7/15

Time taken by Q to complete 7/15 of work = 7/15 × 40 = 56/3 days

= 18 days + 2/3 × 24 = 18 days + 16 hours

**∴ The time taken by Q alone to complete the remaining work after 8 days is 18 days and 16 hours.**

questions.question: Mira can complete a piece of work in 20 days, Nina in 30 days and Sima in 40 days. Mira and Sima worked together for 4 days and then Mira was replaced by Nina. In how many days, altogether, was the work completed?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Mira can complete a piece of work in 20 days.

Nina can complete a piece of work in 30 days.

Sima can complete a piece of work in 40 days.

Mira and Sima worked together for 4 days, then Mira was replaced by Nina.

**Formula Used:**

Work done by a person in 1 day = 1 / (Total days to complete the work)

Total work done = Sum of individual works

**Calculation:**

Work done by Mira in 1 day = 1/20

Work done by Sima in 1 day = 1/40

Work done by Mira and Sima together in 1 day = 1/20 + 1/40

⇒ Work done by Mira and Sima together in 1 day = 2/40 + 1/40

⇒ Work done by Mira and Sima together in 1 day = 3/40

Work done by Mira and Sima in 4 days = 4 × 3/40

⇒ Work done by Mira and Sima in 4 days = 12/40

⇒ Work done by Mira and Sima in 4 days = 3/10

Remaining work = 1 - 3/10

⇒ Remaining work = 10/10 - 3/10

⇒ Remaining work = 7/10

Work done by Nina in 1 day = 1/30

Now, Sima and Nina work together.

⇒ Work done by Sima and Nina together in one day = 1/40 + 1/30

⇒ Work done by Sima and Nina together in one day = 3/120+ 4/120

⇒ Work done by Sima and Nina together in one day = 7/120

Number of days required to complete 7/10 work = 7/10 × 120/7 = 12 days.

Total number of days to complete the work = 4 (Mira and Sima) + 12 (Nina and Sima)

⇒ Total number of days = 16

**The work was completed in 16 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__** 

LCM (20,30,40) = 120 = Total work.

Mira does = 120/20 = 6 units of work in one day.

Nina does = 120/30 = 4 units of work in one day.

Sima does = 120/40 = 3 units of work in one day.

Now, in 4 days Mira and Sima does = 6× 4 + 3× 4 = 36 units of work. 

Remaining work = 120 -36 = 84 units.

After replacement of Mira, Sima and Nina does = 4 + 3 = 7 units in one day.

So, they complete work in 84 / 7 = 12 days.

**∴ The work gets completed in 4 + 12 = 16 days.**
